title: An AI-written article needs no label. Your proofread email gets one
excerpt: The Claude watermark flags text the model only proofread, which the EU AI Act exempts. Meanwhile a fully AI-written article can publish unlabelled.
content_html:
Start with what the mark actually is, because it is not a stamp on the page. When a model writes, it picks each word from a set of reasonable options.

A watermark quietly splits those options into two groups using a secret key, then nudges the model towards one group. One word proves nothing. Across 500 or 1,000 words, a detector holding the key can see the pattern.

Anthropic began marking Claude output on 2 August, worldwide rather than only in Europe. It has not published the algorithm or released a detector.

It marks what Claude touched, not what Claude wrote

This is the part most coverage skipped, and Anthropic states it plainly in its own support article.

A detected mark means the content “may have been processed by Claude”. It does not mean Claude wrote it. Ask the model to proofread, translate or summarise your own writing, and the output carries the mark anyway.

The reverse also holds. No mark does not mean no AI. Short passages, heavy paraphrasing, older models and stripped file metadata all produce clean text that a machine still helped make.

So the signal has two failure directions at once, and the company says so upfront.

The law exempted the grammar fix

Here is where it gets strange. The EU AI Act does not require marking when a system performs an assistive function for standard editing, and the Commission’s own example of that is grammar correction.

Anthropic marks it regardless. Ars Technica called the approach “nuke it from orbit”.

The reason is structural rather than ideological. A watermark applied at the model level cannot distinguish a full draft from a comma. It marks the output, and the output is all it sees.

The result is a mark landing on exactly the content the law was written to leave alone.

And the label almost nobody has to show

Now look at the other half of Article 50, the part that governs what publishers must tell readers. It is far narrower than most people assume.

An AI-written novel needs no label. AI-generated marketing copy needs no label. Text that informs the public on matters of public interest does need one, unless a named and accountable human editor has reviewed it.

Put the two halves together and you get the contradiction. Every keystroke gets watermarked at the model level, while a fully synthetic article can reach readers unlabelled because an editor looked at it.

The EU has been building this machinery for a while. It has already made compulsory labels for synthetic content, and it has given itself powers to inspect and fine models directly. The penalty here runs to €15m or 3% of worldwide annual turnover.

The objections arrived within a day

Investor Bill Gurley argued that if only Anthropic can read the mark, it becomes “judge, jury, and prosecutor”. Anthropic told Business Insider it will ship a free detection API so anyone can check.

Former Microsoft executive Steven Sinofsky raised a different worry. The issue, he wrote, is “data retention and your right to private thoughts free of a digital trail”.

Simon Smith, who runs generative AI at the health agency Klick, asked whether a grammar check would now be flagged as AI-authored. Anthropic’s answer is the one above: the mark shows processing, not authorship.

The software trainer John Crickett asked a sharper question about code. If AI-generated code carries a mark, does that complicate a copyright claim in which the author must show human input?

The case for doing it anyway

The objections are not the whole story. Developer Donn Felker pointed out that marking helps models avoid training on their own output, the problem he called a “snake eating itself”.

Aadit Sheth of The Narrative Company made the reader’s case. Audiences should be able to tell whether the words they are reading reflect a person’s thinking.

The Commission’s own reasoning is broader still. It wants people to calibrate their trust, and it names fraud, impersonation and consumer deception as the risks.

Anthropic frames this as compliance rather than a stance. It is adding marking “to comply with the EU AI Act, and other labs are taking similar steps”, the company said. It also says the watermark does not change the meaning, quality or readability of Claude’s responses.

Some questions remain open. Ars Technica asked the company for a timeline on detection, for any testing on false positives and false negatives, and for how the marks square with the standard-editing exemption.

Anthropic sent a statement that did not address those points. The false-positive rate is the number that matters most here, because it decides how much weight a teacher or an editor should give the mark.

It will not stop anyone who is trying

The uncomfortable part is that the mark catches the honest and misses the deliberate. Paste watermarked text into a second model and ask for a rewrite, and the signal is likely gone.

File-based provenance is weaker still. A screenshot removes it, and so does any competent metadata editor.

The desk has seen this failure before. Meta’s own AI detector missed cropped images, which is roughly the amount of effort involved.

There is also a quiet cost. To keep the statistical signal intact, the model sometimes takes a slightly worse word than the one it would otherwise have chosen.

Anthropic is the only one doing text

This is the commercial risk, and it is real. OpenAI declined to comment specifically to TechRadar and pointed to a support page instead.

That page confirms OpenAI marks images and audio using SynthID and C2PA metadata. On text, it says expanding provenance to all modalities is a goal, as standards and tooling “continue to mature”.

Google uses SynthID too. Neither company has shipped text marking, and both face the same requirement to sell generative systems in the EU.

Existing models have until 2 December to comply. Until then, one lab is carrying the friction alone.

What the law does not touch at all

Article 50 requires disclosure that you are speaking to a machine. It says nothing about what happens to the conversation afterwards.

Stanford researchers reviewed the privacy policies of six major American AI developers. Every one used customer chat data to train by default, and some retained it indefinitely.

So the law now marks the output and ignores the input.

What would settle it

Two things, and both are checkable. The first is the detection API, and specifically its false-positive rate, because a mark on a student’s proofread essay carries the same weight as one on a fabricated news story.

The second is whether OpenAI or Google ship text marking before 2 December, or discover that the standards are still maturing.

Labels already misfire without any of this. X put a “Made with AI” tag on the resignation post of the departing White House press secretary on Wednesday, and then the tag quietly disappeared.

blocks.html_en: The uncomfortable part is that the mark catches the honest and misses the deliberate. Paste watermarked text into a second model and ask for a rewrite, and the signal is likely gone.

sentences.en: The uncomfortable part is that the mark catches the honest and misses the deliberate.
sentences.zh: 令人不舒服的是，标记抓住了诚实的人，却错过了深思熟虑的人。

sentences.en: Paste watermarked text into a second model and ask for a rewrite, and the signal is likely gone.
sentences.zh: 将带水印的文本粘贴到第二个模型中并要求重写，信号可能会消失。

blocks.html_en: File-based provenance is weaker still. A screenshot removes it, and so does any competent metadata editor.

sentences.en: File-based provenance is weaker still.
sentences.zh: 基于文件的来源仍然较弱。

sentences.en: A screenshot removes it, and so does any competent metadata editor.
sentences.zh: 屏幕截图可以删除它，任何有能力的元数据编辑器也可以删除它。

blocks.html_en: The desk has seen this failure before. Meta’s own AI detector missed cropped images, which is roughly the amount of effort involved.

sentences.en: The desk has seen this failure before.
sentences.zh: 办公桌以前就遇到过这种故障。

sentences.en: Meta’s own AI detector missed cropped images, which is roughly the amount of effort involved.
sentences.zh: Meta 自己的人工智能检测器遗漏了裁剪后的图像，这大致就是所涉及的工作量。

blocks.html_en: There is also a quiet cost. To keep the statistical signal intact, the model sometimes takes a slightly worse word than the one it would otherwise have chosen.

sentences.en: There is also a quiet cost.
sentences.zh: 还有一个安静的成本。

sentences.en: To keep the statistical signal intact, the model sometimes takes a slightly worse word than the one it would otherwise have chosen.
sentences.zh: 为了保持统计信号完整，模型有时会采用比原本选择的词稍差的词。

blocks.html_en: Anthropic is the only one doing text

sentences.en: Anthropic is the only one doing text
sentences.zh: Anthropic是唯一做文字的

blocks.html_en: This is the commercial risk, and it is real. OpenAI declined to comment specifically to TechRadar and pointed to a support page instead.

sentences.en: This is the commercial risk, and it is real.
sentences.zh: 这就是商业风险，而且是真实存在的。

sentences.en: OpenAI declined to comment specifically to TechRadar and pointed to a support page instead.
sentences.zh: OpenAI 拒绝专门向 TechRadar 发表评论，而是指出了一个支持页面。

blocks.html_en: That page confirms OpenAI marks images and audio using SynthID and C2PA metadata. On text, it says expanding provenance to all modalities is a goal, as standards and tooling “continue to mature”.

sentences.en: That page confirms OpenAI marks images and audio using SynthID and C2PA metadata.
sentences.zh: 该页面确认 OpenAI 使用 SynthID 和 C2PA 元数据标记图像和音频。

sentences.en: On text, it says expanding provenance to all modalities is a goal, as standards and tooling “continue to mature”.
sentences.zh: 在文字上，它表示随着标准和工具“不断成熟”，扩大所有模式的来源是一个目标。

blocks.html_en: Google uses SynthID too. Neither company has shipped text marking, and both face the same requirement to sell generative systems in the EU.

sentences.en: Google uses SynthID too.
sentences.zh: Google 也使用 SynthID。

sentences.en: Neither company has shipped text marking, and both face the same requirement to sell generative systems in the EU.
sentences.zh: 两家公司都没有推出文本标记，而且两家公司在欧盟销售生成系统都面临着相同的要求。

blocks.html_en: Existing models have until 2 December to comply. Until then, one lab is carrying the friction alone.

sentences.en: Existing models have until 2 December to comply.
sentences.zh: 现有型号必须在 12 月 2 日之前遵守规定。

sentences.en: Until then, one lab is carrying the friction alone.
sentences.zh: 在那之前，一个实验室只能独自承受摩擦力。

blocks.html_en: What the law does not touch at all

sentences.en: What the law does not touch at all
sentences.zh: 法律根本没有触及的事情

blocks.html_en: Article 50 requires disclosure that you are speaking to a machine. It says nothing about what happens to the conversation afterwards.

sentences.en: Article 50 requires disclosure that you are speaking to a machine.
sentences.zh: 第 50 条要求披露您正在与机器交谈。

sentences.en: It says nothing about what happens to the conversation afterwards.
sentences.zh: 它没有提及之后的谈话会发生什么。

blocks.html_en: Stanford researchers reviewed the privacy policies of six major American AI developers. Every one used customer chat data to train by default, and some retained it indefinitely.

sentences.en: Stanford researchers reviewed the privacy policies of six major American AI developers.
sentences.zh: 斯坦福大学的研究人员审查了美国六家主要人工智能开发商的隐私政策。

sentences.en: Every one used customer chat data to train by default, and some retained it indefinitely.
sentences.zh: 每个人都默认使用客户聊天数据进行训练，有些人无限期保留它。

blocks.html_en: So the law now marks the output and ignores the input.

sentences.en: So the law now marks the output and ignores the input.
sentences.zh: 所以现在法律标记了输出并忽略了输入。

blocks.html_en: What would settle it

sentences.en: What would settle it
sentences.zh: 什么可以解决它

blocks.html_en: Two things, and both are checkable. The first is the detection API, and specifically its false-positive rate, because a mark on a student’s proofread essay carries the same weight as one on a fabricated news story.

sentences.en: Two things, and both are checkable.
sentences.zh: 有两件事，两者都是可以检查的。

sentences.en: The first is the detection API, and specifically its false-positive rate, because a mark on a student’s proofread essay carries the same weight as one on a fabricated news story.
sentences.zh: 第一个是检测 API，特别是它的误报率，因为学生校对文章上的标记与捏造的新闻故事上的标记具有相同的权重。

blocks.html_en: The second is whether OpenAI or Google ship text marking before 2 December, or discover that the standards are still maturing.

sentences.en: The second is whether OpenAI or Google ship text marking before 2 December, or discover that the standards are still maturing.
sentences.zh: 第二个问题是 OpenAI 或 Google 是否会在 12 月 2 日之前发布文本标记，或者发现标准仍在成熟中。

blocks.html_en: Labels already misfire without any of this. X put a “Made with AI” tag on the resignation post of the departing White House press secretary on Wednesday, and then the tag quietly disappeared.

sentences.en: Labels already misfire without any of this.
sentences.zh: 如果没有这些，标签就已经失败了。

sentences.en: X put a “Made with AI” tag on the resignation post of the departing White House press secretary on Wednesday, and then the tag quietly disappeared.
sentences.zh: 周三，X 在即将离任的白宫新闻秘书的辞职帖子上贴上了“人工智能制造”的标签，然后这个标签就悄然消失了。

content_html_zh:
从标记的实际含义开始，因为它不是页面上的印记。 当模型写入时，它会从一组合理的选项中选择每个单词。

水印使用密钥悄悄地将这些选项分成两组，然后将模型推向一组。 一句话证明不了什么。 在 500 或 1,000 个单词中，持有密钥的检测器可以看到该模式。

Anthropic 于 8 月 2 日开始在全球范围内（而不仅仅是欧洲）标记克劳德的输出。 它尚未发布算法或发布检测器。

它标记了克劳德所触及的内容，而不是克劳德所写的内容

这是大多数报道都跳过的部分，Anthropic 在其自己的支持文章中明确指出了这一点。

检测到的标记意味着内容“可能已被克劳德处理过”。 这并不意味着克劳德写了它。 让模型校对、翻译或总结你自己的写作，无论如何输出都会带有标记。

反之亦然。 没有标记并不意味着没有AI。 简短的段落、大量的释义、旧模型和剥离的文件元数据都会产生机器仍然帮助制作的干净文本。

因此，该信号同时有两个故障方向，该公司事先是这么说的。

法律免除了语法修正

这就是奇怪的地方。 当系统执行标准编辑的辅助功能时，欧盟人工智能法案并不要求进行标记，委员会自己的例子就是语法纠正。

不管怎样，人择标记了它。 Ars Technica 称这种方法为“将其从轨道上发射出去”。

原因是结构性的而不是意识形态的。 在模型级别应用的水印无法区分完整草稿和逗号。 它标记输出，而输出就是它看到的全部。

结果是在法律规定的内容上留下了一个标记。

而且标签几乎没有人必须展示

现在看看第 50 条的另一半，即规定出版商必须告知读者的内容的部分。 它比大多数人想象的要窄得多。

人工智能写的小说不需要标签。 人工智能生成的营销文案不需要标签。 向公众通报公共利益问题的文本确实需要一个，除非有指定的、负责任的人类编辑对其进行了审查。

把这两部分放在一起，你就会发现矛盾。 每次击键都会在模型级别打上水印，而完全合成的文章可以在没有标签的情况下到达读者手中，因为编辑会查看它。

欧盟建立这一机制已有一段时间了。 它已经对合成内容进行了强制标签，并赋予自己直接检查和罚款模型的权力。 这里的罚款高达 1500 万欧元，即全球年营业额的 3%。

一天之内就收到了反对意见

投资者 Bil​​l Gurley 认为，如果只有 Anthropic 能够读取该标记，它就成为“法官、陪审团和检察官”。 Anthropic 告诉《商业内幕》，它将提供免费的检测 API，以便任何人都可以检查。

微软前高管史蒂文·辛诺夫斯基提出了不同的担忧。 他写道，问题在于“数据保留和您不受数字痕迹影响的私人想法的权利”。

西蒙·史密斯 (Simon Smith) 在健康机构 Klick 负责生成人工智能，他询问语法检查现在是否会被标记为人工智能编写的。 Anthropic 的答案就是上面的答案：标记显示的是处理过程，而不是作者身份。

软件培训师约翰·克里克特（John Crickett）提出了一个关于代码的更尖锐的问题。 如果人工智能生成的代码带有标记，这是否会使作者必须显示人工输入的版权主张变得复杂？

无论如何都要这样做的理由

反对意见并不是故事的全部。 开发人员 Donn Felker 指出，标记有助于模型避免对自己的输出进行训练，他称之为“蛇吃自己”的问题。

The Narrative Company 的阿迪特·谢思 (Aadit Sheth) 为读者提供了案例。 观众应该能够辨别他们正在阅读的文字是否反映了一个人的想法。

委员会自己的推理更为广泛。 它希望人们校准他们的信任，并将欺诈、假冒和消费者欺骗列为风险。

人择将其视为顺从而不是立场。 该公司表示，它正在添加标记“以遵守欧盟人工智能法案，其他实验室也在采取类似的措施”。 它还表示，水印不会改变克劳德回复的含义、质量或可读性。

有些问题仍然悬而未决。 Ars Technica 要求该公司提供检测时间表、对误报和漏报的任何测试，以及这些标记如何与标准编辑豁免相符。

Anthropic 发表了一份声明，但没有解决这些问题。 假阳性率是这里最重要的数字，因为它决定了老师或编辑应该给予分数的权重。

它不会阻止任何尝试的人

令人不舒服的是，标记抓住了诚实的人，却错过了深思熟虑的人。 将带水印的文本粘贴到第二个模型中并要求重写，信号可能会消失。

基于文件的来源仍然较弱。 屏幕截图可以删除它，任何有能力的元数据编辑器也可以删除它。

办公桌以前就遇到过这种故障。 Meta 自己的人工智能检测器遗漏了裁剪后的图像，这大致就是所涉及的工作量。

还有一个安静的成本。 为了保持统计信号完整，模型有时会采用比原本选择的词稍差的词。

Anthropic是唯一做文字的

这就是商业风险，而且是真实存在的。 OpenAI 拒绝专门向 TechRadar 发表评论，而是指出了一个支持页面。

该页面确认 OpenAI 使用 SynthID 和 C2PA 元数据标记图像和音频。 在文字上，它表示随着标准和工具“不断成熟”，扩大所有模式的来源是一个目标。

Google 也使用 SynthID。 两家公司都没有推出文本标记，而且两家公司在欧盟销售生成系统都面临着相同的要求。

现有型号必须在 12 月 2 日之前遵守规定。 在那之前，一个实验室只能独自承受摩擦力。

法律根本没有触及的事情

第 50 条要求披露您正在与机器交谈。 它没有提及之后的谈话会发生什么。

斯坦福大学的研究人员审查了美国六家主要人工智能开发商的隐私政策。 每个人都默认使用客户聊天数据进行训练，有些人无限期保留它。

所以现在法律标记了输出并忽略了输入。

什么可以解决它

有两件事，两者都是可以检查的。 第一个是检测 API，特别是它的误报率，因为学生校对文章上的标记与捏造的新闻故事上的标记具有相同的权重。

第二个问题是 OpenAI 或 Google 是否会在 12 月 2 日之前发布文本标记，或者发现标准仍在成熟中。

如果没有这些，标签就已经失败了。 周三，X 在即将离任的白宫新闻秘书的辞职帖子上贴上了“人工智能制造”的标签，然后这个标签就悄然消失了。
